rationale: This is a cosmetic operator swap on the archived PayablesAccelerationShortDebtDrain (DELTA → TS_RANK of the identical apalch/sale leg with the identical dlc/sale-plus-cash-drain gate), not a substantively different mechanism.

The accrual leg and distress gate are literally identical to the archived PayablesCashBufferShortDebtStress; only the gate-flip on the short side was removed, which is a structural cosmetic change rather than a new economic hypothesis for a leg that already produced a negligible ls_alpha.

Fourth variant of the same MA(3) unfunded-inventory leg (after InventoryFundingGapDistressSpread, SmoothedInventoryLiquidityTrap, InventoryPayablesDeficitMonotone) with only the leverage scaler changed to dltt/sale, and it re-asserts a negative sign despite the closest prior variant delivering a significant *positive* alpha (t = +2.81) that the proposal never reconciles.

The sign convention on recch/invch is handled correctly and the sign-flipped "liquidity relief vs. obfuscation" reading of the earlier gross-complexity alphas is a genuinely different economic hypothesis, though the directional leg is close to the classic working-capital accruals anomaly conditioned on distress and the MIN-with-magnitude construction makes the driver hard to attribute.

A fourth |aoloch| opacity variant differing from prior archive entries only by an operator (TS_RANK) and a gate substitution, with no diagnosis of why the earlier opacity legs repeatedly produced wrong-signed portfolio evidence; the non-directional ABS leg also conflates income-increasing and income-decreasing accruals.

The dominance ratio is essentially identical to the archived NonDepAccrualDominanceUnderDebt (dp → dpc) with only the distress gate swapped, and the hypothesis claims a directional bearish effect from a purely absolute-magnitude ratio, which is internally inconsistent and ignores the prior version's opposite-signed alpha.
